chapter_theme: Acting well begins before the act: weighing cost and return, taking counsel, and matching the means to the person and to one's own position. The chapter's vocabulary is that of a careful ledger, and its fear is less of failure than of being laughed at for failing.
structure_note: Parimelazhagar's divisions: which deed to do and how (461-462), which to avoid and the cost of not avoiding it (463-465), do and don't stated together (466), then the means and to whom they suit (467-470).

461.reading: Weigh what will be lost, what will arise, and the gain that comes of it later, and then act.
461.nuance: The verse separates the immediate return from later gain. Parimelazhagar draws out the consequence: a deed that only breaks even now may still be worth doing if the later gain is there. So this is not a plain cost-benefit rule.

462.reading: Nothing is out of reach for those who act after examining it with chosen company and considering it themselves.
462.nuance: Parimelazhagar takes the two verbs in order: first with the company, then alone. So consulting doesn't replace judgment. தெரிந்த also makes the counsellors themselves the first thing chosen.

463.reading: Those with understanding don't undertake a deed that loses the capital for the sake of gain.
463.nuance: Parimelazhagar's example is political: marching to take another's land and losing one's own. He also reads செய்வினை as covering even work already begun, so sunk effort is no excuse.

464.reading: Those who fear the affliction called disgrace don't begin what isn't clear to them.
464.nuance: The stated motive is shame, not loss. Parimelazhagar explains தொடங்கார்: once begun, a thing can't be dropped midway, so scorn would be added to the failure.

465.reading: Rising up without thinking through every aspect is one way of bedding your enemy in good soil.
465.nuance: பாத்தி is a garden bed. The sting is that the hasty attacker does the enemy's cultivating for them: a failed attack strengthens its target.

466.reading: One perishes by doing what is unfit to do, and perishes too by not doing what is fit.
466.nuance: Omission gets the same verdict as commission. தக்க is not obviously moral: Parimelazhagar's list of the unfit includes the too-laborious, the useless and the doubtful, which makes it prudential.

467.reading: Think and then resolve on a task; to say 'we'll think after resolving' is a lapse.
467.nuance: What is to be thought about isn't stated. For Parimelazhagar it is the means, the four strategies; for Manakkudavar it is the result. The first assumes the deed is already chosen.

468.reading: Effort not made in the right way will collapse, even if many stand by to protect it.
468.nuance: The verse corrects the chapter 45 picture of allies as near-sufficient: support can't save effort that is on the wrong path. Parimelazhagar spells out which means suit which kind of person.

469.reading: Even in doing good there is error, when it is done without knowing each person's character.

positions.position: நன்று is the good stratagem, gifts and sweet words, used on rival kings, and the error is that the task fails.
positions.quote: வேற்று வேந்தர் மாட்டு நன்றான உபாயம் செய்தற்கண்ணும் குற்றம் உண்டாம்;

positions.position: நன்று is kindness to anyone, and misjudged kindness comes back as harm.

470.reading: Think and do what won't be scorned; the world doesn't accept what doesn't accord with oneself.

positions.position: The issue is tactical fit: the strong shouldn't use the means of the weak, such as gifts, and the weak shouldn't use force.
positions.quote: தாம் வலியராய் வைத்து மெலியார்க்கு உரிய கொடுத்தல் முதலிய மூன்றனைச் செய்தலும்,

positions.position: The issue is propriety: even if a thing can be accomplished, do only what others won't despise.
positions.quote: முடியுமாயினும், பிறராலிகழப்படாதவற்றை எண்ணிச் செய் தல் வேண்டும்;

links.note: Both use முதல், capital, from the merchant's world. 449 applies it to allies and 463 to risk: a king's ledger has two different kinds of principal that he can't afford to lose.
656 forbids what the worthy condemn even if one's mother is starving, the most extreme form of Manakkudavar's reading here, that being able to succeed doesn't excuse scorned means.
464 says to avoid beginning what isn't clear. 469 adds that even with the deed and intent clear, the person is another thing to know. Clarity about the act is not clarity about the recipient.
